evidence.excerpt: title: Rendering-Free Event Frame Simulation for Fast Reinforcement Learning of Autonomous Robot Navigation; submitted: 2026-10-27; categories: cs.RO; authors: Dequan Ou; Austin Lopez; Quentin Missinne; Christophe De Wagter; Guido C. H. E. de Croon; abstract: Event cameras offer low latency, high dynamic range, and milliwatt-level power consumption, making them ideal for agile robots such as tiny drones navigating through cluttered environments. However, existing simulators generally render photorealistic images before converting them into events, making large-scale reinforcement learning prohibitively slow. We propose an analytic event simulator that exploits what event cameras fundamentally measure - moving contrast edges - to synthesize event streams directly from scene geometry and ego-motion without visual rendering. Our simulator generates a 64x64 event observation in 17 microseconds on a single GPU - over 400x faster than a state-of-the-art rendering pipeline - enabling end-to-end reinforcement learning for goal-directed obstacle avoidance to converge in under 30 minutes - three orders of magnitude faster than training on rendered events.
